Objective: Assess and diagnose the patient presenting with excessively dry skin that has been persistent since childhood.
Patient: 8-year-old boy
History: The patient has had dry, scaly skin since he was 6 months old, according to his mother. The condition worsens in the winter and mildly improves during the summer months. The patient does not report itching, redness, or any discharge associated with the dryness.
Symptoms: Primary: Generalized fine scales with coarse skin all over the body; Secondary: Lack of involvement in skin creases, Multiple papular elevations at the base of hair follicles, Darkening of palmar and plantar creases
Past Medical History: No significant past medical history.
Social History: The patient is a school-going child. Lives with parents and one younger sibling. No similar skin conditions noted in the family.
Review of Systems: Denies any associated symptoms such as itching, redness, or secretion from the areas with dry skin.
Physical Examination:
- Vital Signs: Temperature: 36.8°C (98°F), Blood_Pressure: 100/60 mmHg, Heart_Rate: 80 bpm, Respiratory_Rate: 18 breaths/min
- Skin_Examination: Inspection: Generalized dryness with fine scaling noted over most of the body. Skin creases of the neck and cubital and popliteal fossae are spared.; Palpation: Skin texture is coarse across affected areas. Multiple papular elevations noted at the base of hair follicles. Darkening is observed in the palmar and plantar creases.
Test Results:
- Skin_Biopsy: Histopathological examination shows compact hyperkeratosis and reduced or absent granular layer, consistent with the clinical diagnosis.
- Blood_Tests: Complete_Blood_Count: Within normal limits; Thyroid_Function_Tests: Within normal limits
- Allergy_Testing: Negative for common allergens
